key_insight: A phone-based chatbot grounded in regional context and designed for code-mixed, short queries can feasibly deliver safer, more usable maternal health information in low-resource settings by combining multilingual understanding with a safety-focused triage layer.
problem_solved: Addresses the challenge of providing trustworthy maternal health information when user queries are short, underspecified, code-mixed across languages, and lack symptom context—making correct, safe routing and region-specific answers difficult.
method: Design a phone-first conversational agent that handles code-mixed inputs and very short utterances using multilingual intent/entity models and context augmentation.
Ground answers in region-specific clinical guidance and deploy a safety/triage module that detects risk, requests minimal clarifying prompts, and routes high-risk cases to human care.
Evaluate the system in realistic low-resource conditions (phone interactions, low health literacy) to measure information accuracy, safety of routing, and user usability.
impact: Provides a practical blueprint for building safe, region-aware conversational agents for sensitive health domains; highlights the importance of multilingual robustness, minimal clarifying prompts, and explicit triage for deployment in low-resource clinical settings.
visual_elements: Conversation flowchart showing: user short/code-mixed query → intent/entity extraction → regional grounding → safety triage → response or human referral
Icon row depicting phone UI, multilingual/code-mixed bubbles, and a clinician handoff to emphasize modalities and escalation
Bar/stacked chart comparing outcomes (accuracy, safe referrals, user satisfaction) across baseline vs. the proposed system
Map or regional overlay illustrating how answers are grounded in local clinical guidance and resources
paper_title: Developing and evaluating a chatbot to support maternal health care
paper_authors: Smriti Jha, Vidhi Jain, Jianyu Xu, Grace Liu, Sowmya Ramesh
